records.source: בֵּאדַ֛יִן דָּרְיָ֥וֶשׁ מַלְכָּ֖א שָׂ֣ם טְעֵ֑ם וּבַקַּ֣רוּ׀בְּבֵ֣ית סִפְרַיָּ֗א דִּ֧י גִנְזַיָּ֛א מְהַחֲתִ֥ין תַּמָּ֖ה בְּבָבֶֽל׃
records.gloss: Then Darius the king made a decree, and they searched in [the] house of the scrolls where the treasures [were] deposited, there in Babylon.
pieces: Then King Darius issued an order, and a search was made in the archives where the treasures were stored in Babylon.

L.1: Then Darius the king issued a decree, and they searched in the house of the scrolls, where the treasures were stored, there in Babylon.

R.1: So King Darius gave an order, and his officials searched the royal records kept in the treasure house in Babylon.

decisions.choice: the house of the scrolls where the treasures were stored: the royal archive
decisions.reason: Persian kings kept official documents, written on scrolls and tablets, in their treasuries along with valuables. This is the place Tattenai asked the king to search (5:17).

decisions.choice: they searched: the king's officials made the search
decisions.reason: The Aramaic says only "they"; it means the officials who carried out the king's order. Balanced uses a passive and Readable names the officials.

decisions.choice: the archives (B); the royal records (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "the house of the scrolls" was.

records.heading: Darius finds the decree of Cyrus

records.source: וְהִשְׁתְּכַ֣ח בְּאַחְמְתָ֗א בְּבִֽירְתָ֛א דִּ֛י בְּמָדַ֥י מְדִינְתָּ֖ה מְגִלָּ֣ה חֲדָ֑ה וְכֵן־כְּתִ֥יב בְּגַוַּ֖הּ דִּכְרוֹנָֽה׃פ
records.gloss: And was found in Achmetha, in the fortress which [is] in Media the province, a scroll, one, and thus [it was] written in it: A memorandum:
pieces: A scroll was found in the fortress at Ecbatana in the province of Media, and this was written in it: "Memorandum:

L.2: And a scroll was found at Ecbatana, in the fortress that is in the province of Media, and thus it was written in it: "A memorandum:

R.2: A scroll was found in the fortress city of Ecbatana in the province of Media. This is what was written on it: "Official record:

decisions.choice: Ecbatana in Media: the Persian kings' summer capital
decisions.reason: The Aramaic name of the city is Achmetha; in Greek it is Ecbatana (modern Hamadan in Iran). It was the old capital of Media, where the Persian kings stayed in the summer. Cyrus was there in his first year, which explains why the record was found there and not in Babylon, where the search began.

decisions.choice: a memorandum: a record of a royal decision for the archive
decisions.reason: The word means a record kept to remind. What follows (verses 3-5) is not the proclamation read to the people (1:2-4) but the official note of the king's decision, with the building's measurements and the payment from the treasury.

decisions.choice: Ecbatana
decisions.reason: The Aramaic form Achmetha is less known than the Greek name Ecbatana, by which the city is known in history; every level uses Ecbatana and the decision gives the Aramaic form.

records.source: בִּשְׁנַ֨ת חֲדָ֜ה לְכ֣וֹרֶשׁ מַלְכָּ֗א כּ֣וֹרֶשׁ מַלְכָּא֮ שָׂ֣ם טְעֵם֒ בֵּית־אֱלָהָ֤א בִֽירוּשְׁלֶם֙ בַּיְתָ֣א יִתְבְּנֵ֔א אֲתַר֙ דִּֽי־דָבְחִ֣ין דִּבְחִ֔ין וְאֻשּׁ֖וֹהִי מְסֽוֹבְלִ֑ין רוּמֵהּ֙ אַמִּ֣ין שִׁתִּ֔ין פְּתָיֵ֖הּ אַמִּ֥ין שִׁתִּֽין׃
records.gloss: In year one of Cyrus the king, Cyrus the king made a decree: [The] house of God in Jerusalem, the house let it be built, [the] place where they sacrifice sacrifices, and its foundations [be] retained; its height sixty cubits, its width sixty cubits,
pieces: In the first year of King Cyrus, the king issued a decree concerning the house of God in Jerusalem: Let the house be rebuilt as a place where sacrifices are offered, and let its foundations be laid firmly. Its height shall be {{units:about 90 feet|sixty cubits}} and its width {{units:about 90 feet|sixty cubits}},

L.3: In the first year of Cyrus the king, Cyrus the king issued a decree: As for the house of God in Jerusalem, let the house be built, the place where they offer sacrifices, and let its foundations be firmly laid; its height sixty cubits [and] its width sixty cubits,

R.3: In his first year as king, King Cyrus gave this order about God's temple in Jerusalem: The temple must be rebuilt as a place for offering sacrifices. Its foundations must be laid firmly. It is to be {{units:about 90 feet|sixty cubits}} high and {{units:about 90 feet|sixty cubits}} wide,

decisions.choice: let its foundations be firmly laid
alternatives: let the old foundations be kept
decisions.reason: The participle is rare and its sense is uncertain. It most likely means that the foundations are to be laid so as to bear the building; it may instead mean that the old foundations are to be kept and built on. The words are also sometimes read as part of the description of the place of sacrifice. Every reading has the house rebuilt where it stood.

decisions.choice: sixty cubits high and sixty wide: larger than Solomon's temple, with no length given
decisions.reason: Solomon's temple was thirty cubits high and twenty wide (1 Kings 6:2). The length is missing, and the figures may set the greatest size the king would pay for rather than a plan. The returned exiles in fact built a house that older people thought poor beside the first (3:12; Haggai 2:3).

decisions.choice: the place where they offer sacrifices: the house is a place of worship
decisions.reason: The decree names the purpose of the house: sacrifices to the God of heaven, which Darius will order paid for (verses 9-10).

decisions.choice: {{units:about 90 feet|sixty cubits}}
decisions.reason: A cubit is about 18 inches, so sixty cubits is about 90 feet. Literal keeps the cubit.

records.source: נִדְבָּכִ֞ין דִּי־אֶ֤בֶן גְּלָל֙ תְּלָתָ֔א וְנִדְבָּ֖ךְ דִּי־אָ֣ע חֲדַ֑ת וְנִ֨פְקְתָ֔א מִן־בֵּ֥ית מַלְכָּ֖א תִּתְיְהִֽב׃
records.gloss: courses of stone of rolling, three, and a course of timber new; and the cost from [the] house of the king let it be given.
pieces: with three layers of large stones and one layer of new timber. The cost is to be paid from the royal treasury.

L.4: with three layers of huge stones and one layer of new timber; and let the cost be paid from the king's house.

R.4: with three rows of huge stones and one row of new wooden beams. The cost is to be paid from the king's treasury.

decisions.choice: three courses of stone and one of timber: the building method of the temple
decisions.reason: The same way of building is described for Solomon's inner court (1 Kings 6:36; 7:12) and in the officials' report (5:8). It may describe the whole wall, repeated in layers, or a single section; the text does not say.

decisions.choice: stone of rolling: large stones (see 5:8)
decisions.reason: As in 5:8, stones so large they were rolled into place.

decisions.choice: the cost from the king's house: the royal treasury pays
decisions.reason: Persian kings supported the temples of their subject peoples. Cyrus's decree in 1:4 called on others to give; this record shows that the crown itself undertook the cost, which Darius confirms from the province's taxes (verse 8).

decisions.choice: the royal treasury (B); the king's treasury (R)
decisions.reason: "The king's house" here means his treasury, the money of the crown.

records.source: וְ֠אַף מָאנֵ֣י בֵית־אֱלָהָא֮ דִּ֣י דַהֲבָ֣ה וְכַסְפָּא֒ דִּ֣י נְבֽוּכַדְנֶצַּ֗ר הַנְפֵּ֛ק מִן־הֵיכְלָ֥א דִי־בִירוּשְׁלֶ֖ם וְהֵיבֵ֣ל לְבָבֶ֑ל יַהֲתִיב֗וּן וִ֠יהָךְ לְהֵיכְלָ֤א דִי־בִירֽוּשְׁלֶם֙ לְאַתְרֵ֔הּ וְתַחֵ֖ת בְּבֵ֥ית אֱלָהָֽא׃ס
records.gloss: And also the vessels of [the] house of God of gold and silver, which Nebuchadnezzar brought out from the temple which [was] in Jerusalem and carried to Babylon, let them return and go to the temple which [is] in Jerusalem, to its place; and you shall deposit [them] in [the] house of God.
pieces: Also, the gold and silver vessels of the house of God, which Nebuchadnezzar took from the temple in Jerusalem and brought to Babylon, are to be given back and taken to the temple in Jerusalem, each to its proper place. You shall put them in the house of God."

L.5: And also let the vessels of gold and silver of the house of God, which Nebuchadnezzar took out of the temple that was in Jerusalem and brought to Babylon, be returned and go to the temple that is in Jerusalem, each to its place; and you shall put them in the house of God."

R.5: Also, the gold and silver objects from God's temple, which Nebuchadnezzar took from the temple in Jerusalem and brought to Babylon, must be given back. They are to be taken back to the temple in Jerusalem, and each one is to be put in its proper place in God's temple."

decisions.choice: the vessels Nebuchadnezzar took: their return already told in 1:7-11 and 5:14-15
decisions.reason: The memorandum confirms what the elders said in their answer (5:14-15) and what chapter 1 records: the vessels were handed over to Sheshbazzar to be taken back.

decisions.choice: you shall deposit them: the memorandum turns to address the one responsible
decisions.reason: The verb is singular "you". The record speaks to the official in charge of the return, Sheshbazzar (5:14-15), as an order would.

decisions.choice: each one is to be put in its proper place in God's temple
decisions.reason: Readable joins the two phrases about the vessels' place and leaves out the change to "you", which Literal and Balanced keep.

records.source: כְּעַ֡ן תַּ֠תְּנַי פַּחַ֨ת עֲבַֽר־נַהֲרָ֜ה שְׁתַ֤ר בּוֹזְנַי֙ וּכְנָוָ֣תְה֔וֹןאֲפַרְסְכָיֵ֔א דִּ֖י בַּעֲבַ֣ר נַהֲרָ֑ה רַחִיקִ֥ין הֲו֖וֹ מִן־תַּמָּֽה׃
records.gloss: Now, Tattenai, governor of Beyond the River, Shethar-bozenai and their colleagues, the officials who [are] in Beyond the River, far be from there.
pieces: "Now therefore, Tattenai, governor of Beyond the River, Shethar-bozenai and your colleagues, the officials of the province Beyond the River: keep away from there.

L.6: "Now, Tattenai, governor of Beyond the River, Shethar-bozenai and their colleagues, the officials who are in Beyond the River: keep far away from there.

R.6: Then King Darius sent this reply: "Tattenai, governor of the province west of the Euphrates, and Shethar-bozenai and your fellow officials there: Stay away from that place.

decisions.choice: now: the king's reply begins without an opening
decisions.reason: The writer moves from the record found in the archive straight into Darius's letter, leaving out its address and greeting. "Now" in letters marks the turn to business (as 4:13, 14; 5:17).

decisions.choice: the officials: as in 5:6
decisions.reason: The same Persian title as in 5:6; its exact sense is uncertain.

decisions.choice: be far from there: do not interfere
decisions.reason: The king does not order the officials out of Jerusalem; he tells them to keep their hands off the work, as verse 7 explains.

decisions.choice: Then King Darius sent this reply
decisions.reason: Readable says who is now speaking, since the Aramaic moves without notice from the old record to Darius's letter (m1).

records.heading: Darius orders the work to go on

records.source: שְׁבֻ֕קוּ לַעֲבִידַ֖ת בֵּית־אֱלָהָ֣א דֵ֑ךְ פַּחַ֤ת יְהוּדָיֵא֙ וּלְשָׂבֵ֣י יְהוּדָיֵ֔א בֵּית־אֱלָהָ֥א דֵ֖ךְ יִבְנ֥וֹן עַל־אַתְרֵֽהּ׃
records.gloss: Leave the work of this house of God; [the] governor of the Jews and [the] elders of the Jews, this house of God let them build on its place.
pieces: Let the work on this house of God go on. Let the governor of the Jews and the elders of the Jews rebuild this house of God on its site.

L.7: Leave the work on this house of God alone; let the governor of the Jews and the elders of the Jews build this house of God on its place.

R.7: Do not interfere with the work on this temple of God. Let the governor of the Jews and their leaders rebuild it where it stood before.

decisions.choice: the governor of the Jews: Zerubbabel
decisions.reason: Haggai calls Zerubbabel governor of Judah (Haggai 1:1; 2:2). Darius does not name him; the letter recognizes his office.

decisions.choice: leave: let alone, do not hinder
decisions.reason: The verb means to leave or let be. It is the opposite of the stop Tattenai could have imposed (5:5).

decisions.choice: Let the work go on (B); Do not interfere with (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "leave the work" means: the officials are not to hinder it.

records.source: וּמִנִּי֮ שִׂ֣ים טְעֵם֒ לְמָ֣א דִֽי־תַֽעַבְד֗וּן עִם־שָׂבֵ֤י יְהוּדָיֵא֙ אִלֵּ֔ךְ לְמִבְנֵ֖א בֵּית־אֱלָהָ֣א דֵ֑ךְ וּמִנִּכְסֵ֣י מַלְכָּ֗א דִּ֚י מִדַּת֙ עֲבַ֣ר נַהֲרָ֔ה אָסְפַּ֗רְנָא נִפְקְתָ֛א תֶּהֱוֵ֧א מִֽתְיַהֲבָ֛א לְגֻבְרַיָּ֥א אִלֵּ֖ךְ דִּי־לָ֥א לְבַטָּלָֽא׃
records.gloss: And from me a decree is made concerning what you shall do with these elders of the Jews to build this house of God: and from the property of the king, which [is] the tribute of Beyond the River, diligently the cost let it be given to these men, that [they] not be made to cease.
pieces: Moreover, I issue a decree about what you are to do for these elders of the Jews in rebuilding this house of God: the cost is to be paid to these men in full from the royal revenue, from the taxes of the province Beyond the River, so that the work will not stop.

L.8: And I make a decree concerning what you shall do with these elders of the Jews for the building of this house of God: from the king's property, from the tribute of Beyond the River, let the cost be paid to these men diligently, so that they are not stopped.

R.8: I also order you to help these leaders of the Jews rebuild this temple of God. Pay their costs in full from the royal taxes collected in your province, so that the work does not stop.

decisions.choice: the tribute of Beyond the River: the province's taxes owed to the king
decisions.reason: The officials who questioned the building now have to pay for it out of the taxes they collected for the crown. It is a reversal of the threat in 4:13, where unpaid tribute was the charge against the Jews.

decisions.choice: diligently: promptly and in full
decisions.reason: The Persian loanword of 5:8 here governs the payment: it is to be made exactly and without delay.

decisions.choice: that they not be stopped: so the work does not cease
decisions.reason: The clause can mean that the men are not to be held up, or that the work is not to cease for lack of funds; the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: royal revenue (B); royal taxes (R)
decisions.reason: The "king's property" here is the revenue from the province, as the next phrase says.

records.source: וּמָ֣ה חַשְׁחָ֡ן וּבְנֵ֣י תוֹרִ֣ין וְדִכְרִ֣ין וְאִמְּרִ֣ין׀לַעֲלָוָ֣ן׀לֶאֱלָ֪הּ שְׁמַיָּ֟א חִנְטִ֞ין מְלַ֣ח׀חֲמַ֣ר וּמְשַׁ֗ח כְּמֵאמַ֨ר כָּהֲנַיָּ֤א דִי־בִירֽוּשְׁלֶם֙ לֶהֱוֵ֨א מִתְיְהֵ֥ב לְהֹ֛ם י֥וֹם׀בְּי֖וֹם דִּי־לָ֥א שָׁלֽוּ׃
records.gloss: And whatever is needed, both young bulls and rams and lambs for burnt offerings to the God of the heavens, wheat, salt, wine and oil, according to [the] word of the priests who [are] in Jerusalem, let it be given to them day by day without fail,
pieces: Whatever is needed, whether young bulls, rams or lambs for burnt offerings to the God of heaven, or wheat, salt, wine or oil, as the priests in Jerusalem request, must be given to them every day without fail,

L.9: And whatever is needed, young bulls, rams and lambs for burnt offerings to the God of heaven, wheat, salt, wine and oil, as the priests who are in Jerusalem say, let it be given to them day by day without fail,

R.9: Every day, give the priests in Jerusalem whatever they ask for: young bulls, rams and lambs for burnt offerings to the God of heaven, and wheat, salt, wine and olive oil. Do not fail to do this,

decisions.choice: burnt offerings with wheat, salt, wine and oil: the daily sacrifices of the temple
decisions.reason: The law required animals offered with flour mixed with oil and with wine poured out (Numbers 28:3-8), and salt with every offering (Leviticus 2:13). The king provides everything the daily worship needs.

decisions.choice: according to the word of the priests: the priests decide what is needed
decisions.reason: The amounts are left to the priests. Ezra 7:21-22 records a similar grant by Artaxerxes, with limits set.

decisions.choice: Every day ... Do not fail to do this
decisions.reason: Readable puts the instruction first and the list after it, and makes "without fail" a command of its own.

records.source: דִּֽי־לֶהֱוֺ֧ן מְהַקְרְבִ֛ין נִיחוֹחִ֖ין לֶאֱלָ֣הּ שְׁמַיָּ֑א וּמְצַלַּ֕יִן לְחַיֵּ֥י מַלְכָּ֖א וּבְנֽוֹהִי׃
records.gloss: that they may be offering pleasing offerings to the God of the heavens and praying for [the] life of the king and his sons.
pieces: so that they may offer sacrifices pleasing to the God of heaven and pray for the life of the king and his sons.

L.10: so that they may offer pleasing sacrifices to the God of heaven and pray for the life of the king and his sons.

R.10: Then they can offer sacrifices that please the God of heaven, and pray for me and my sons.

decisions.choice: pleasing offerings: sacrifices whose smoke rises as a soothing aroma
decisions.reason: The word comes from the phrase "a soothing aroma to the LORD" (Leviticus 1:9; Numbers 28:2): offerings that God accepts with favor.

decisions.choice: pray for the life of the king and his sons: the king's interest in the temple
decisions.reason: Persian kings asked for prayers for themselves and their house in the temples they supported, as Cyrus did in Babylon. Jeremiah had told the exiles to pray for the welfare of the city where they lived (Jeremiah 29:7).

decisions.choice: pray for me and my sons
decisions.reason: Readable lets the king speak of himself in the first person; the Aramaic uses the formal "the king".

records.source: וּמִנִּי֮ שִׂ֣ים טְעֵם֒ דִּ֣י כָל־אֱנָ֗שׁ דִּ֤י יְהַשְׁנֵא֙ פִּתְגָמָ֣א דְנָ֔ה יִתְנְסַ֥ח אָע֙ מִן־בַּיְתֵ֔הּ וּזְקִ֖יף יִתְמְחֵ֣א עֲלֹ֑הִי וּבַיְתֵ֛הּ נְוָל֥וּ יִתְעֲבֵ֖ד עַל־דְּנָֽה׃
records.gloss: And from me a decree is made that every person who alters this word, let a beam be pulled out from his house, and lifted up let him be impaled on it, and his house a refuse heap let it be made on account of this.
pieces: I also decree that if anyone alters this order, a beam is to be pulled from his house and he is to be impaled on it, and his house is to be made a rubbish heap for this offense.

L.11: And I make a decree that anyone who alters this word, let a beam be pulled from his house, and let him be lifted up and impaled on it, and let his house be made a refuse heap because of this.

R.11: I also give this order: If anyone changes this command, a beam is to be pulled out of his house. He will be lifted up and stuck on it to die, and his house will be turned into a garbage dump.

decisions.choice: impaled on a beam from his own house: the Persian punishment for defying the king
decisions.reason: Impaling was a known Persian punishment for rebels; Darius's own inscription at Behistun records it. Haman's death in Esther 7:9-10 is the same kind of punishment. The penalty shows how seriously the king guarded his decree.

decisions.choice: a refuse heap: a place of dung and rubbish
decisions.reason: The word is used of a heap of rubbish or dung (also Daniel 2:5; 3:29). The man's house is not only destroyed but made unclean and worthless.

decisions.choice: alters this word: changes or disobeys this order
decisions.reason: The verb means to change. It covers both altering the decree and acting against it, as verse 12 says of anyone who reaches out to destroy the house.

decisions.choice: lifted up and stuck on it to die
decisions.reason: Readable explains what impaling is, without more detail than the text gives.

records.source: וֵֽאלָהָ֞א דִּ֣י שַׁכִּ֧ן שְׁמֵ֣הּ תַּמָּ֗ה יְמַגַּ֞ר כָּל־מֶ֤לֶךְ וְעַם֙ דִּ֣י׀יִשְׁלַ֣ח יְדֵ֗הּ לְהַשְׁנָיָ֛ה לְחַבָּלָ֛ה בֵּית־אֱלָהָ֥א דֵ֖ךְ דִּ֣י בִירוּשְׁלֶ֑ם אֲנָ֤ה דָרְיָ֨וֶשׁ֙ שָׂ֣מֶת טְעֵ֔ם אָסְפַּ֖רְנָא יִתְעֲבִֽד׃פ
records.gloss: And the God who has caused his name to dwell there, may he overthrow every king and people who will stretch out his hand to alter, to destroy this house of God which [is] in Jerusalem. I, Darius, have made a decree; diligently let it be done.
pieces: May the God who has made {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name dwell there overthrow any king or people who reaches out a hand to change this or to destroy this house of God in Jerusalem. I, Darius, have issued this decree. Let it be carried out with all diligence."

L.12: And may the God who has caused {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name to dwell there overthrow any king or people who stretches out a hand to alter [this], to destroy this house of God that is in Jerusalem. I, Darius, have issued a decree; let it be carried out diligently."

R.12: God has chosen that temple as the place where people worship {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. May {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} destroy any king or nation that tries to change this order or to destroy that temple in Jerusalem. I, Darius, have given this order. Carry it out carefully and completely."

decisions.choice: caused his name to dwell there: the language of Deuteronomy
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy speaks of the place the LORD would choose "to make his name dwell there" (Deuteronomy 12:11; 14:23). Darius uses words the Jews would know, perhaps from those who drafted the letter; the writer of Ezra hears in them God's own claim on the house.

decisions.choice: may God overthrow any king or people: a curse to protect the decree
decisions.reason: Royal decrees and inscriptions of the time often ended with a curse on anyone who would undo them. Darius calls on the God of the temple himself to defend it.

decisions.choice: diligently: as in verse 8
decisions.reason: The same Persian word as in 5:8 and 6:8, 13.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name; may {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}
decisions.reason: Pronouns for God take the deity_pronoun setting, even in a Persian king's letter, since they refer to Israel's God.

decisions.choice: God has chosen that temple as the place where people worship him
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom of God's name dwelling in a place: he chose it as the place where he is worshiped and known.

records.source: אֱ֠דַיִן תַּתְּנַ֞י פַּחַ֧ת עֲבַֽר־נַהֲרָ֛ה שְׁתַ֥ר בּוֹזְנַ֖י וּכְנָוָתְה֑וֹן לָקֳבֵ֗ל דִּֽי־שְׁלַ֞ח דָּרְיָ֧וֶשׁ מַלְכָּ֛א כְּנֵ֖מָא אָסְפַּ֥רְנָא עֲבַֽדוּ׃
records.gloss: Then Tattenai, governor of Beyond the River, Shethar-bozenai and their colleagues, according to what Darius the king had sent, thus diligently they did.
pieces: Then Tattenai, governor of Beyond the River, Shethar-bozenai and their colleagues carried out with diligence what King Darius had ordered.

L.13: Then Tattenai, governor of Beyond the River, Shethar-bozenai and their colleagues did diligently just as Darius the king had sent [word].

R.13: So Tattenai, the governor of the province west of the Euphrates, Shethar-bozenai and the other officials did exactly what King Darius had ordered.

decisions.choice: diligently: they obeyed promptly and in full
decisions.reason: The narrator uses the king's own word (verse 12) to say that the order was carried out as given.

decisions.choice: according to what Darius had sent: the king's letter
decisions.reason: The phrase means in line with the message Darius sent; Literal supplies "word".

records.heading: The house of God is finished and dedicated

records.source: וְשָׂבֵ֤י יְהוּדָיֵא֙ בָּנַ֣יִן וּמַצְלְחִ֔ין בִּנְבוּאַת֙ חַגַּ֣י נְבִיָּ֔א וּזְכַרְיָ֖ה בַּר־עִדּ֑וֹא וּבְנ֣וֹ וְשַׁכְלִ֗לוּ מִן־טַ֨עַם֙ אֱלָ֣הּ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וּמִטְּעֵם֙ כּ֣וֹרֶשׁ וְדָרְיָ֔וֶשׁ וְאַרְתַּחְשַׁ֖שְׂתְּא מֶ֥לֶךְ פָּרָֽס׃
records.gloss: And the elders of the Jews [were] building and prospering through [the] prophesying of Haggai the prophet and Zechariah son of Iddo; and they built and finished according to [the] decree of the God of Israel and according to [the] decree of Cyrus and Darius and Artaxerxes king of Persia.
pieces: So the elders of the Jews went on building and made good progress, encouraged by the prophesying of Haggai the prophet and Zechariah son of Iddo. They finished the building by the command of the God of Israel and by the decrees of Cyrus, Darius and Artaxerxes, kings of Persia.

L.14: And the elders of the Jews were building and prospering through the prophesying of Haggai the prophet and Zechariah son of Iddo. And they built and finished by the decree of the God of Israel and by the decree of Cyrus and Darius and Artaxerxes king of Persia.

R.14: The leaders of the Jews kept on building, and the work went well because the prophets Haggai and Zechariah son of Iddo encouraged them. They finished the temple, just as the God of Israel had commanded and as Cyrus, Darius and Artaxerxes, the kings of Persia, had ordered.

decisions.choice: the decree of God and the decree of the kings: one word for both
decisions.reason: The same Aramaic word is used for God's command and the kings' decrees. The writer sets them side by side: the Persian kings' orders carried out what the God of Israel had already decided.

decisions.choice: Artaxerxes: a later king, named for his support of the temple
decisions.reason: Artaxerxes I (465-424 BC) reigned after the temple was finished in 515 BC. He is included because he later gave gifts for the temple and its worship (7:15-24, 27). The writer names together all the Persian kings who helped God's house, not only those of this chapter.

decisions.choice: king of Persia: a title for each of the three kings
decisions.reason: The singular title is attached to the last name, but each of the three was king of Persia; Balanced and Readable say "kings".

decisions.choice: went on building and made good progress, encouraged by (B); kept on building ... because the prophets encouraged them (R)
decisions.reason: "Through the prophesying" means the prophets' messages gave the builders the will to go on (5:1-2); Balanced and Readable say so.

records.source: וְשֵׁיצִיא֙ בַּיְתָ֣ה דְנָ֔ה עַ֛ד י֥וֹם תְּלָתָ֖ה לִירַ֣ח אֲדָ֑ר דִּי־הִ֣יא שְׁנַת־שֵׁ֔ת לְמַלְכ֖וּת דָּרְיָ֥וֶשׁ מַלְכָּֽא׃פ
records.gloss: And was finished this house by day three of [the] month Adar, which was year six of [the] reign of Darius the king.
pieces: This house was completed on the third day of the month of Adar, in the sixth year of the reign of King Darius.

L.15: And this house was finished on the third day of the month Adar, which was the sixth year of the reign of Darius the king.

R.15: The temple was finished on the third day of the month of Adar, in the sixth year that Darius was king.

decisions.choice: the third day of Adar in Darius's sixth year: about March 515 BC
decisions.reason: Adar is the twelfth month, in late winter. Darius's sixth year ran from the spring of 516 to the spring of 515 BC, so the temple was finished about seventy years after it was destroyed in 587/586 BC, and about four and a half years after the work began again (4:24; Haggai 1:15).

decisions.choice: the sixth year that Darius was king
decisions.reason: Readable puts "the reign of" in plain words.

records.source: וַעֲבַ֣דוּ בְנֵֽי־יִ֠שְׂרָאֵל כָּהֲנַיָּ֨א וְלֵוָיֵ֜א וּשְׁאָ֣ר בְּנֵי־גָלוּתָ֗א חֲנֻכַּ֛ת בֵּית־אֱלָהָ֥א דְנָ֖ה בְּחֶדְוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And made the sons of Israel, the priests and the Levites and the rest of the sons of the exile, [the] dedication of this house of God with joy.
pieces: Then the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, the priests, the Levites and the rest of the returned exiles celebrated the dedication of this house of God with joy.

L.16: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, the priests and the Levites and the rest of the {{gender:children|sons}} of the exile, celebrated the dedication of this house of God with joy.

R.16: Then the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} joyfully celebrated the dedication of God's temple. The priests, the Levites and all the other people who had come back from exile took part.

decisions.choice: the sons of Israel ... the sons of the exile: the returned community as Israel
decisions.reason: The people who came back from Babylon were mostly from Judah, Benjamin and Levi (1:5), yet they are called Israel. They saw themselves as the continuation of the whole people, as the twelve offerings in verse 17 show.

decisions.choice: dedication: the first act of worship in the new house
decisions.reason: The word is used for the dedication of the altar (Numbers 7:10) and of Solomon's temple (2 Chronicles 7:5, 9). The later festival of Hanukkah takes its name from the same word.

decisions.choice: the returned exiles (B); the people who had come back from exile (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide wording for "the sons of the exile".

records.source: וְהַקְרִ֗בוּ לַחֲנֻכַּת֮ בֵּית־אֱלָהָ֣א דְנָה֒ תּוֹרִ֣ין מְאָ֔ה דִּכְרִ֣ין מָאתַ֔יִן אִמְּרִ֖ין אַרְבַּ֣ע מְאָ֑ה וּצְפִירֵ֨י עִזִּ֜ין לְחַטָּאָ֤ה עַל־כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ תְּרֵֽי־עֲשַׂ֔ר לְמִנְיָ֖ן שִׁבְטֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And they offered for [the] dedication of this house of God bulls, one hundred; rams, two hundred; lambs, four hundred; and he-goats of goats for a sin offering for all Israel, twelve, according to [the] number of [the] tribes of Israel.
pieces: For the dedication of this house of God they offered 100 bulls, 200 rams and 400 lambs, and as a sin offering for all Israel, twelve male goats, one for each of the tribes of Israel.

L.17: And they offered for the dedication of this house of God 100 bulls, 200 rams, 400 lambs, and as a sin offering for all Israel twelve male goats, according to the number of the tribes of Israel.

R.17: To dedicate God's temple they offered 100 bulls, 200 rams and 400 lambs. They also offered twelve male goats, one for each tribe of Israel, as a sin offering for all the people of Israel.

decisions.choice: 100 bulls, 200 rams, 400 lambs: a modest offering beside Solomon's
decisions.reason: At the dedication of the first temple Solomon offered 22,000 cattle and 120,000 sheep (1 Kings 8:63). The smaller number fits a small and poor community; the writer records it without apology.

decisions.choice: twelve goats for a sin offering for all Israel: one for each tribe
decisions.reason: Though few of the twelve tribes were present, the offering was made for the whole people, as when the tribal leaders brought twelve offerings at the first altar (Numbers 7:87). It expresses the hope that all Israel would be restored.

records.source: וַהֲקִ֨ימוּ כָהֲנַיָּ֜א בִּפְלֻגָּתְה֗וֹן וְלֵוָיֵא֙ בְּמַחְלְקָ֣תְה֔וֹן עַל־עֲבִידַ֥ת אֱלָהָ֖א דִּ֣י בִירוּשְׁלֶ֑ם כִּכְתָ֖ב סְפַ֥ר מֹשֶֽׁה׃פ
records.gloss: And they set the priests in their divisions and the Levites in their sections over [the] service of God which [is] in Jerusalem, according to [the] writing of [the] book of Moses.
pieces: They appointed the priests by their divisions and the Levites by their groups for the service of God in Jerusalem, as it is written in the book of Moses.

L.18: And they appointed the priests in their divisions and the Levites in their sections for the service of God that is in Jerusalem, as it is written in the book of Moses.

R.18: They also put the priests and the Levites into their groups to take turns serving God at the temple in Jerusalem, as the book of Moses says.

decisions.choice: as written in the book of Moses: the service follows the law
decisions.reason: The law of Moses sets the priests and Levites apart for the service of God and gives each their duties (Numbers 3-4; 8; 18). The division of the priests into twenty-four groups that served in turn goes back to David (1 Chronicles 23-24). The writer says that the worship of the new house was ordered according to the law.

decisions.choice: divisions and sections: groups that served in turn
decisions.reason: Two words for the groups into which the priests and the Levites were organized, each serving at the temple for a set period.

decisions.choice: to take turns serving
decisions.reason: Readable says what the divisions were for (m2).

records.source: וַיַּעֲשׂ֥וּ בְנֵי־הַגּוֹלָ֖ה אֶת־הַפָּ֑סַח בְּאַרְבָּעָ֥ה עָשָׂ֖ר לַחֹ֥דֶשׁ הָרִאשֽׁוֹן׃
records.gloss: And kept the sons of the exile the Passover on [the] fourteenth of the month, the first.
pieces: On the fourteenth day of the first month, the returned exiles celebrated the Passover.

L.19: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of the exile kept the Passover on the fourteenth [day] of the first month.

R.19: On the fourteenth day of the first month, the people who had come back from exile celebrated the Passover.

decisions.choice: the text returns from Aramaic to Hebrew
decisions.reason: From 4:8 to 6:18 Ezra is written in Aramaic, the language of the Persian empire's letters and records. With this verse the narrative goes back to Hebrew, as the account turns from the letters of officials and kings to Israel's own worship. Aramaic returns at 7:12 for Artaxerxes's letter.

decisions.choice: Passover on the fourteenth of the first month: as the law commands
decisions.reason: The law sets Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month, Nisan, in the spring (Exodus 12:6; Leviticus 23:5). The temple was finished in Adar, the month before (verse 15), so this was the first Passover kept at the new house, about six weeks later.

decisions.choice: the returned exiles (B); the people who had come back from exile (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide wording for "the sons of the exile".

records.heading: The returned exiles keep the Passover

records.source: כִּ֣י הִֽטַּהֲר֞וּ הַכֹּהֲנִ֧ים וְהַלְוִיִּ֛ם כְּאֶחָ֖ד כֻּלָּ֣ם טְהוֹרִ֑ים וַיִּשְׁחֲט֤וּ הַפֶּ֨סַח֙ לְכָל־בְּנֵ֣י הַגּוֹלָ֔ה וְלַאֲחֵיהֶ֥ם הַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים וְלָהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: For had purified themselves the priests and the Levites as one, all of them [were] clean; and they slaughtered the Passover for all the sons of the exile and for their brothers the priests and for themselves.
pieces: The priests and the Levites had purified themselves together; all of them were ceremonially clean. The Levites slaughtered the Passover lambs for all the returned exiles, for their fellow priests and for themselves.

L.20: For the priests and the Levites had purified themselves as one; all of them were clean. And they slaughtered the Passover for all the {{gender:children|sons}} of the exile, and for their brothers the priests, and for themselves.

R.20: The priests and the Levites had all made themselves ceremonially clean, ready for worship. The Levites killed the Passover lambs for all the people who had come back from exile, for the priests and for themselves.

decisions.choice: they slaughtered: the Levites, for the people, the priests and themselves
decisions.reason: "Their brothers the priests" shows that the ones slaughtering were the Levites, who did this at the Passovers of Hezekiah and Josiah (2 Chronicles 30:17; 35:11). The ordinary worshipers, who might not be ritually clean, were spared the task.

decisions.choice: purified as one; all clean: ready to serve at the feast
decisions.reason: Being clean in the law's sense was a condition for keeping Passover (Numbers 9:6-13). At Hezekiah's Passover not enough priests had purified themselves (2 Chronicles 30:3); here all had, which the writer notes as a sign that things were done rightly.

decisions.choice: the Passover: the Passover lamb
decisions.reason: The same word names the feast and the animal sacrificed for it (Exodus 12:21).

decisions.choice: The Levites; lambs
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the Levites as the subject (m1) and say "Passover lambs" for the animals (m3).

decisions.choice: ceremonially clean
decisions.reason: "Clean" here is the ritual purity the law required for worship, not physical cleanness.

records.source: וַיֹּאכְל֣וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל הַשָּׁבִים֙ מֵֽהַגּוֹלָ֔ה וְכֹ֗ל הַנִּבְדָּ֛ל מִטֻּמְאַ֥ת גּוֹיֵֽ־הָאָ֖רֶץ אֲלֵהֶ֑ם לִדְרֹ֕שׁ לַֽיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And ate the sons of Israel who had returned from the exile, and everyone who had separated himself from the uncleanness of the nations of the land to them, to seek Yahweh, God of Israel.
pieces: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} who had returned from exile ate it, together with all who had separated themselves from the uncleanness of the nations of the land to join them in seeking {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel.

L.21: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel who had returned from the exile ate [it], and every [one] who had separated {{gender:themselves|himself}} from the uncleanness of the nations of the land to [join] them, to seek {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel.

R.21: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} who had come back from exile ate the Passover meal. Others joined them too: people who had turned away from the unclean practices of the nations living in the land, so that they could worship {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel.

decisions.choice: everyone who had separated himself ... to them: others who joined the returned exiles
alternatives: Israelites who had stayed in the land
decisions.reason: These are people who were not among the returned exiles but turned from the ways of the land's peoples to join Israel in worship. They may have been Israelites who had stayed in the land during the exile, or people of other nations who became part of Israel. The law allowed an outsider who was circumcised to keep Passover (Exodus 12:48).

decisions.choice: the uncleanness of the nations: their idolatry and practices against the law
decisions.reason: Uncleanness here is the impurity of worshiping other gods and of practices the law forbids (compare 9:1, 11). To separate from it was to commit oneself to the LORD alone.

decisions.choice: to seek the LORD: to worship him and turn to him
decisions.reason: Seeking the LORD means turning to him in worship and obedience (Deuteronomy 4:29; 2 Chronicles 15:12-13), not looking for something lost.

decisions.choice: worship
decisions.reason: Readable says what seeking the LORD means here (m3).

records.source: וַיַּֽעֲשׂ֧וּ חַג־מַצּ֛וֹת שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִ֖ים בְּשִׂמְחָ֑ה כִּ֣י׀שִׂמְּחָ֣ם יְהוָ֗ה וְֽהֵסֵ֞ב לֵ֤ב מֶֽלֶךְ־אַשּׁוּר֙ עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם לְחַזֵּ֣ק יְדֵיהֶ֔ם בִּמְלֶ֥אכֶת בֵּית־הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃פ
records.gloss: And they kept [the] feast of unleavened bread seven days with joy, for had made them joyful Yahweh and had turned [the] heart of [the] king of Assyria toward them, to strengthen their hands in [the] work of [the] house of God, [the] God of Israel.
pieces: For seven days they joyfully celebrated the Festival of Unleavened Bread, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had filled them with joy and had changed the attitude of the king of Assyria toward them, so that he supported them in the work on the house of God, the God of Israel.

L.22: And they kept the Feast of Unleavened Bread seven days with joy, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had made them joyful and had turned the heart of the king of Assyria toward them, to strengthen their hands in the work of the house of God, the God of Israel.

R.22: For seven days they celebrated the Festival of Bread Without Yeast with great joy. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} had made them very happy, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had made the king of Assyria friendly toward them. The king had helped them in the work of rebuilding the temple of the God of Israel.

decisions.choice: the Feast of Unleavened Bread: the seven days after Passover
decisions.reason: The law joins the seven-day feast to Passover, from the fifteenth to the twenty-first of the first month (Exodus 12:15-20; Leviticus 23:6-8), in memory of leaving Egypt in haste.

decisions.choice: the king of Assyria: the Persian king, ruler of the lands Assyria once held
decisions.reason: Darius was king of Persia, but he ruled the former Assyrian empire, and the old name could be used for the ruler of that region. It also makes a point: the power that once destroyed the northern kingdom (2 Kings 17:6) now helped to rebuild God's house.

decisions.choice: the LORD made them joyful and turned the king's heart: God behind the king's decree
decisions.reason: The writer sees the king's change of mind as the LORD's work, as he did with Cyrus (1:1; compare Proverbs 21:1). The joy of the feast is joy at what God had done.

decisions.choice: to strengthen their hands: to support and encourage them
decisions.reason: Strengthening someone's hands means giving them help and courage to do a task (Nehemiah 2:18; 6:9).

decisions.choice: Festival of Unleavened Bread (B); Festival of Bread Without Yeast (R)
decisions.reason: Readable explains "unleavened" in plain words.
